tickerText: [TENNIS] Sunday quarter-finals at the China Open and Japan Open: Alexander Zverev meets six-time Beijing champion Novak Djokovic (7 p.m.), Daniil Medvedev faces Francisco Cerundolo, and defending Tokyo champ Carlos Alcaraz takes on Denis Shapovalov at 1 p.m. • [SQUASH] PSA Swedish Open finals day on the GIH glass court in Stockholm: top seeds Fayrouz Aboelkheir vs Georgina Kennedy (2 p.m.) and Mohamad Zakaria vs Joel Makin (3 p.m.) after Saturday's semis • [BADMINTON] VICTOR BWF World Junior Team Championships open Monday in Cairo—the first African host since 2002—with nine continental teams and new 3×55 relay scoring for the Suhandinata Cup • [PICKLEBALL] Championship Sunday at the Rate Las Vegas Open (10 a.m. PT, PickleballTV/Tennis Channel): five 1,000-point finals at Darling Tennis Center as Anna Leigh Waters can hit career PPA title No. 200 with two doubles wins • [TABLE TENNIS] WTT China Smash main draw begins at Shougang Park with men's and women's singles round of 64 plus mixed doubles round of 24; Wang Chuqin and Felix Lebrun head the $2.05M season finale

newsItems.title: Zverev–Djokovic Headline Beijing QFs
newsItems.excerpt: Alexander Zverev's 6-0, 6-3 rout of Juncheng Shang sets a Sunday night China Open quarter-final with Novak Djokovic, while Daniil Medvedev, Alex de Minaur, and Hubert Hurkacz also bid for the ATP 500 semis in Beijing.

newsItems.title: Stockholm Finals On Glass Court
newsItems.excerpt: The Champion Fiberglass Swedish Open closes Oct. 4 at GIH with women's final Aboelkheir–Kennedy and men's Zakaria–Makin after Kennedy rallied past Amanda Sobhy and Fayrouz Aboelkheir swept Nele Gilis in Saturday semis.

newsItems.title: Vegas Open Crowns Five Champions
newsItems.excerpt: The Carvana PPA Tour's Rate Las Vegas Open finishes Oct. 4 with best-of-three finals in every division on PickleballTV; Anna Leigh Waters—skipping singles—needs women's and mixed doubles titles to reach 200 career PPA wins.

newsItems.title: China Smash Main Draw Opens
newsItems.excerpt: The WTT China Smash 2026 moves from qualifying into round-of-64 singles and mixed-doubles round of 24 on Oct. 4 at Shougang Park, with world No. 1 Wang Chuqin, Felix Lebrun, and a 64-player women's field chasing 2,000 ranking points.
